title: How I kept cool with NYC's free battery program for window AC units
gist: Startup Every Electric loaned free 2 kWh batteries to about 1,000 NYC households in summer 2026 so window ACs could keep running during peak demand while earning Con Edison demand-response payments, aggregating to about 4 MWh of distributed storage. It plans to exceed 10,000 batteries in 2027 and is eyeing other utility territories.

insights.claim: Every Electric loans batteries to renters for a deposit cut from $50 to $30, sells them outright at $650 each, and splits Con Edison demand-response earnings with households, using the revenue to pay off the batteries and grow the fleet.
insights.speaker: Jeremy Hsu
insights.so_what: A revenue-share, capex-light distribution model lowers the barrier for residential storage among renters, a segment normally excluded from home batteries.
insights.quote: you essentially share in the value that you provide in the grid

insights.claim: Every Electric generally promises residents about $150 per year per air conditioner through Con Edison's Smart Usage Rewards program, and is paid directly by Con Edison as a program partner.
insights.speaker: Jeremy Hsu
insights.so_what: Utility-paid per-device incentives are the revenue basis for virtual power plant startups, so program continuity and rates are key risks.

insights.claim: The founders, former Columbia postdocs, launched in 2023 as Standard Potential Co. to commercialize sodium-ion batteries, then pivoted to deploying residential batteries as a virtual power plant and rebranded in 2026.
insights.speaker: Jeremy Hsu
insights.so_what: A deep-tech battery chemistry startup found a business in deployment and services using off-the-shelf lithium iron phosphate cells, a pattern of value shifting to the grid-services layer.

insights.claim: Every Electric went from 100 batteries across 65 households in summer 2025 to 2,000 batteries across about 1,000 households in 2026, equal to four megawatt-hours of storage.
insights.speaker: Jeremy Hsu
insights.so_what: A 20x unit jump in one year shows fast deployment, though 4 MWh remains tiny relative to utility-scale storage.
insights.locator: From dozens to thousands of batteries

insights.claim: The wait list reached requests for more than 15,000 batteries last summer, and the company aims to deploy more than 10,000 batteries in 2027.
insights.speaker: Jeremy Hsu
insights.so_what: Strong demand with a free offer, but the 2027 target is a company aim and depends on utility program funding.

insights.claim: New York City has more than 2 million rental homes and over 80 percent of housing is more than 50 years old, typically relying on window air conditioners instead of central air, creating a large addressable base for plug-in batteries.
insights.speaker: Jeremy Hsu
insights.so_what: Old building stock without central AC makes behind-the-meter distributed storage a plausible peak-shaving tool in dense cities.

insights.claim: Wang says new utility territories are approaching the company, seeing that megawatt-hours of storage can be drop-shipped to customers, and the company is looking at mapping the model to new markets.
insights.speaker: Andrew Wang
insights.so_what: Utilities may treat distributed drop-shipped storage as an alternative to building peaker or utility-scale capacity.
insights.quote: you can drop-ship literal megawatt hours to customers as a solution
insights.locator: Every Electric remains focused on New York City

insights.claim: Wang frames the fleet as taking one typical four-megawatt-hour containerized utility battery block and breaking it into 1,000 pieces spread across the city.
insights.speaker: Andrew Wang
insights.so_what: Aggregated behind-the-meter batteries can replicate grid-scale storage capacity without siting or interconnection of large projects.
insights.quote: So we've sort of taken that up and broken it up into 1,000 pieces spread across the city.
insights.locator: From dozens to thousands of batteries

insights.claim: The program let the author's household run window ACs through a triple-digit heat dome while still taking part in demand response, whereas earlier summers required precooling and sweating through the event periods.
insights.speaker: Jeremy Hsu
insights.so_what: Storage removes the comfort tradeoff that limits demand response participation, potentially raising enrolment and grid relief at peaks.

insights.claim: The battery is the Bluetti Elite 200 V2, a lithium iron phosphate unit storing 2 kWh that works with any 120V plug-in air conditioner and can also provide backup power for routers or refrigerators.
insights.speaker: Jeremy Hsu
insights.so_what: The model runs on commodity consumer power stations, so margins depend on hardware cost declines and firmware rather than proprietary cells.

insights.claim: When Con Edison reduced voltage for hundreds of thousands of customers to protect grid equipment during extreme heat, battery draw tripped the author's circuit breaker twice, which Every Electric addressed with firmware updates.
insights.speaker: Jeremy Hsu
insights.so_what: Old wiring and grid voltage reductions are real operating risks that could limit scale and raise support costs.

insights.claim: Wang says each household is unique, with pre-war buildings having old wiring, so the company must account for losses on both the Con Edison side and in building walls to tune each power bank.
insights.speaker: Andrew Wang
insights.so_what: Per-home tuning adds operational complexity, which can strain unit economics as the fleet scales.
insights.quote: Every household is unique, and sometimes you have pre-war buildings with old wiring
